bullets.text: Q2 CR 93.3, YTD 92.9; net income up 174% for Q2 and 68% YTD; comprehensive income increased 154% in Q2 and 9% YTD, eliminating timing differences in recognized investment gains and losses.

Written premium grew 6% in Q2 and 7% YTD. Average premiums reflecting year-ago rate changes were a big driver of premium growth, but application growth was considerably slower than prepared to handle.

Comfortable with prior-year aggregate rate actions; implemented modest downward rate adjustments in major states including Florida where loss experience was very good, though personal injury protection coverage uncertainty persists.

Application growth was considerably slower than prepared to handle; renewal offer acceptances experienced an expected decline with slow recovery, particularly among policies in early-term relationships.

Customer demand strengthened and was healthy across both channels; Direct Auto new applications rose by low single digits YOY, while Agency channel new applications lagged the prior-year quarter by roughly 7%.

Catastrophe losses reached $130M YTD, comparable to the prior two years; severe weather events were manageable within product pricing, though Colorado Springs fires forced temporary evacuation of an operating facility.

Portfolio total return was 2.2% YTD (down from 2.9% through May); short duration positioning and front-end yield curve exposure provided some insulation against rising interest rates and yield curve steepening.
Snapshot advertising campaign outside the Superstore construct ran most of Q2 to highlight driving profile subsidies; performance was very acceptable but short of breakout.

Snapshot and Progressive Home Advantage remained key growth initiatives; Snapshot reached 1.2M policies and $1.8B in premium; Commercial Auto aggregate results matched expectations despite greater period-to-period volatility.
Opening nine Service Centers with co-located claims offices in 2013, adding sites in NJ and CA; rest-of-year focus targets customer retention, multi-product growth, and claims and cost advantages.
